title: How Far Can Web Architecture Go Toward Zero Tokens?
kicker: Web architecture, measured by Fielding’s own words
html:
How Far Can Web Architecture Go Toward Zero Tokens?

Web architecture, measured by Fielding’s own words. Have you ever paid a model to find the same path twice?

The driver The three R’s The hype

The measuring stick
say: Have you ever paid a model to find the same path twice? Most of us have, this year, many times a day. Kelsey Hightower gave that habit a name and an alternative: Zero Token Architecture. Infer once, then run the result without a model. So here's the question for the next half hour. How far can Web architecture go toward that? Not one person's vision: the architecture the Web already runs on. And we need a measuring stick, so we'll use Roy Fielding's own words: his 2000 dissertation, his 2008 rules, and his complaints about what people did with them. Every colored pill you see is a mark on that stick, and you can click any of them, any time. Tokens are only part of why it matters. The business needs three R's: repeatability, right behavior, and resilience. Reasoning is the part everyone's excited about. We'll keep it at the edges.
